resources.string: Stops every vibration a game asks for: rumble, trigger rumble and haptics. Leave it off unless you want no vibration at all.
In controller mouse mode, holding X moves the pointer in fixed pixel steps, for small targets. Each press of Y doubles the step, from 1 to 128 pixels.
Alt+Tab, the Windows key and similar go to the PC instead of this device, where Android allows it. Turn it off to keep those shortcuts on this device.
System keys only in full screen
In a window, Alt+Tab, the Windows key and similar stay with this device; in full screen they go to the PC. Turn on to switch apps beside a windowed stream.
A physical keyboard’s Back key sends the Windows key to the PC instead of Back or Esc. Android’s Back gesture and the stream menu hotkey still open the stream menu.
Right Alt sends the Windows key, which a Mac uses as Command. Leave it off if you type characters with AltGr: Right Alt then no longer works as AltGr.
Opens the on-screen keyboard when you select a text field on the PC and closes it after. Needs a PC that reports text fields; turn off to open it yourself.
Shows the buttons, sticks, triggers, rumble, lights and motion a controller sends.
Press buttons and move the sticks. The D-pad and A also move around this page; hold B or Back for one second to leave.
Connect a controller and press any button.
Disable rumble is on, so streams will not vibrate. These tests still do.
Touch the touchpad to see where.
Nightjar reads a wired Switch Pro Controller itself, so gyro, rumble, Home and Capture work. Android asks for USB access in a stream; Bluetooth controllers and Joy-Con stay on Android’s input.
No USB access; the Switch Pro Controller stays on Android’s input.\nReconnect the cable to retry.
